quest.title: A Sliver of Hope
quest.description: Though you and Yoimiya managed to secure Sakujirou's passage out by sea, he wavers, unable to reconcile himself to his wish. It is at this moment that Yoimiya recalls an old couple among Naganohara Fireworks' clients who might be able to help him out.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

talks.objective: Visit the old couple to ask for their help

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Kaori
dialogues.text: Well! If it isn't Yoimiya! Come on in, dear, come and take a seat.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Kaori
dialogues.text: Are these two your friends?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Yes, they're travelers from afar. Outsiders have a very difficult time getting into Inazuma nowadays.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Saburou
dialogues.text: Indeed, these are unprecedented times. But seeing as they came all this way, we locals should give them a warm welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm. Oh, before I forget — I brought the fireworks that you ordered.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Saburou
dialogues.text: Oh, thank you, dear. Your family is so good to us, every year. First your father, and now you.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Saburou
dialogues.text: I wonder if I'll still be alive to see the next heir of Naganohara Fireworks.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Of course you will, you're both in great health! Don't say things like that, it's bad luck.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Kaori
dialogues.text: *sigh* We aren't as young as we once were, though. The body knows it.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Kaori
dialogues.text: It used to be that I could spend all day working the land, carrying water back and forth, but now, even a moment of light work leaves me with all sorts of aches and pains.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Kaori
dialogues.text: I wanted to do some weeding yesterday, but as soon as I bent down to get started, I suddenly felt that if I went any further, I wouldn't be able to get back up again.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: No worries, say no more — we'll handle it!

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Saburou
dialogues.text: No, no, no, we can't be putting you to work when you're a guest in our home.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Saburou
dialogues.text: I'll just go fetch the tea and some snacks, and then we'll continue our conversation.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: It's fine, it's not like it's the first time I've helped you with chores. I just haven't had much time recently with the fireworks show coming up — but once that's outta the way, I'll be sure to come by more often.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's no trouble, really. We don't mind helping.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Kaori
dialogues.text: *sigh* You're such good kids... As for mine, he's all grown up now, hasn't found anyone yet, and he doesn't visit very often.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Kaori
dialogues.text: If you're quite sure it's no trouble, then... I have some pickled radish here, would you mind delivering it to Satoru on the other side of the village?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Sure, it won't take us a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: The old folks aren't very mobile, so c'mon, let's help them out. We'll <color=#00E1FFFF>get rid of the weeds</color> first and then <color=#00E1FFFF>deliver the pickled radish</color>.

dialogues.speaker: Satoru
dialogues.text: The Naganohara Fireworks Show must be coming up soon, right? My daughter left quite a while ago.

dialogues.speaker: Satoru
dialogues.text: Heh, she couldn't get out the house quickly enough. She's clearly very taken with this boy in the city, it was written all over her face...

dialogues.speaker: Satoru
dialogues.text: *sigh* But, at least she's happy, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Saburou
dialogues.text: I'm sorry that we weren't much help.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Kaori
dialogues.text: One day, though, that child is going to have to face up to his feelings.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Kaori
dialogues.text: This is one life lesson that he can't learn from his parents.

talks.objective: Help the old couple clean up their courtyard
Give the Pickled Radish to Satoru in the village

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hey, Satoru, how have you been? Keeping well?

dialogues.speaker: Satoru
dialogues.text: Same as usual, not much has changed. You're looking full of life, as always.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: All thanks to the support of our loyal customers. The family business just keeps getting better and better.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: We sold some fireworks to Liyue a while back, and word is they were a real hit. So it looks like we'll be getting more business from over there in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Satoru
dialogues.text: That must mean a lot more work for you though? Are you sure you and Mr. Ryuunosuke can manage?

dialogues.speaker: Satoru
dialogues.text: If it gets too much, don't forget you can always ask me for help. Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: We should be fine. I think we can cope.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh yeah, um, this is some Pickled Radish from Mrs. Imatani.

dialogues.speaker: Satoru
dialogues.text: Wow, thank you so much! I never used to be a fan of Pickled Radish, would you believe.

dialogues.speaker: Satoru
dialogues.text: But then I tried some of Mrs. Imatani's homemade stuff, and I couldn't get enough of it. It's a family staple now.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Speaking of your family, how is everyone doing?

dialogues.speaker: Satoru
dialogues.text: They're doing well. We have the occasional heated argument, but... I guess that's every family ever.

dialogues.speaker: Satoru
dialogues.text: Being close to family is better than never getting to see them, even if it does mean putting up with some conflict.

dialogues.speaker: Satoru
dialogues.text: Now, Mr. and Mrs. Imatani seem to have a great relationship — but still, they must get lonely with their child never visiting.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Huh, they didn't seem that way to me. I think they're just used to it.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: You make a good point though. I should drop by more often in the future. That way, they won't get so bored.

dialogues.speaker: Satoru
dialogues.text: I'm sure they'd love that — as would all of us in Konda Village. You're always welcome here.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Hee-hee, thank you.

talks.objective: Report back to the old couple

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Kaori
dialogues.text: That was quick! Ah, young people are so handy.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Younger people have bundles of energy, and older people have a wealth of wisdom. Each have their strengths.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Saburou
dialogues.text: Speaking of youth... Do you know what? It's been 50 years this year.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Kaori
dialogues.text: Oh, so it has! Goodness, how the time flies... You barely notice as the years go by, but then suddenly, 50 years have passed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: 50 years since what? Some important day?

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Saburou
dialogues.text: Haha, well, if you must know, it was 50 years ago, back in the days when this young lady was still trying to win me over, that—

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Kaori
dialogues.text: Oh, stop trying to impress them. We both know you were the one who was hopelessly smitten and desperately trying to win my affection...

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Saburou
dialogues.text: Well, maybe you're right. 50 years ago, I proposed to my wife at the Naganohara Fireworks Show. We've been together ever since.

response.speaker: Imatani Saburou
response.text: To tell the truth, I was still a little uncertain. I wasn't sure what I was doing when I walked into the Naganoharas' shop and ordered my firework.

response.speaker: Imatani Saburou
response.text: Even as it was rising up into the sky... I still had no clue what I was going to say.

response.speaker: Imatani Saburou
response.text: But then it exploded... the sky lit up... I looked back at her and saw her eyes, twinkling in the light of the fireworks...

response.speaker: Imatani Saburou
response.text: ...Before I knew what was happening, apparently, I'd already said it, and well, she'd said yes.

response.speaker: Imatani Kaori
response.text: 50 years... In some ways, it's a long time, in others, it's no time at all. Really, it's just a number.

response.speaker: Imatani Kaori
response.text: But 50 years of being together... now that is something worth commemorating.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I had no idea it was your 50th anniversary. If I'd known, I would've made some extra-fancy fireworks, just for you.

response.speaker: Imatani Kaori
response.text: Oh, no, it's quite alright. We always set off the same firework every year. It wouldn't be the same without it.

response.speaker: Imatani Kaori
response.text: Seeing that firework go off takes us right back to those days. Even at this age, we still look back with not a single regret.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw, what a great relationship they have...

response.speaker: Imatani Saburou
response.text: Enough about us, though. Yoimiya, aren't you busy with the fireworks show coming up? Was there something you needed to discuss?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Yeah, um... it's a difficult thing to talk about, but here goes...

response.speaker: Imatani Saburou
response.text: Hmm... Sakujirou... so, he came back.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Huh? You know him?

response.speaker: Imatani Kaori
response.text: He was our boy's best friend when they were young.

response.speaker: Imatani Kaori
response.text: *sigh* They were inseparable. They grew up together, shared everything with each other, and went everywhere together.

response.speaker: Imatani Kaori
response.text: But one day, they had a terrible argument...

response.speaker: Imatani Saburou
response.text: Sakujirou seemed to feel that Inazuma was too peaceful, and wanted to see what the outside world was like.

response.speaker: Imatani Saburou
response.text: But our Keisuke took after his father and mother. He felt that there was nothing wrong at all with being peaceful.

response.speaker: Imatani Saburou
response.text: You know what children are like, they get terribly worked up about these sorts of things. In the end, Sakujirou stormed off, and that was that.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I see...

response.speaker: Imatani Saburou
response.text: Keisuke said nothing to me or my wife about the fight. We could sense that he was very hurt by it, but he didn't want to talk with us about how he was really feeling.

response.speaker: Imatani Saburou
response.text: Eventually, whether out of pent-up anger or for some other reason, he joined the Tenryou Commission. He rarely comes home anymore.

response.speaker: Imatani Kaori
response.text: If it was anything else, I could talk to Keisuke, and I'm sure he'd be willing to help.

response.speaker: Imatani Kaori
response.text: But since it's Sakujirou... I don't feel there's any way we can get involved.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What a strange coincidence. Who'd have thought...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I understand now. When I asked Sakujirou why he came back, he just said "because of past mistakes" and wasn't willing to elaborate.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Now, I finally understand why he can't decide what to do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Two best buddies in childhood... one grows up to join the Tenryou Commission, the other grows up to join the Tenryou Commission's most wanted list...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Well, no worries, if that's the case then never mind.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: We can find some other way to help Sakujirou, there's no need to make things difficult for you. This sounds like something for Sakujirou and Keisuke to resolve between themselves.

response.speaker: Imatani Kaori
response.text: Yes, it'd be so nice if they could go back to the way things were.

response.speaker: Imatani Saburou
response.text: I think after all these years, they ought to let go of their grudges.

choices.text: I never would have imagined it either.
You should be very proud of what you have.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Yoimiya, something bad's happened! Some people from the Tenryou Commission came by.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Huh? Why? ...Do they know?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Pops, are you alright? They didn't do anything to you, did they?

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: I told them the show was starting soon and the place was filled with fireworks, so they shouldn't go in because it's a fire hazard.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: But they didn't listen. It seemed like they knew Sakujirou was inside.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Luckily, Sakujirou heard them coming in time and managed to escape through the window. The Tenryou Commission wasn't able to capture him.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: This is bad news. I don't think Sakujirou had enough time to make his mind up...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Pops, did you see where he went?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: The Tenryou Commission will definitely be chasing after him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you catch any of their names?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Good point! Names, we need names! Suddenly showing up like this, surely it must be Keisuke's doing!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: The Commission wouldn't normally cause this big of a fuss over a stowaway.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Sorry, my ears are no good, and I didn't get a good look at them either. If you're wondering which way they went, they left the city.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: I wish I caught their names... *sigh* But I didn't hear a thing...

dialogues.speaker: Morihiko
dialogues.text: As it happens, I did.

dialogues.speaker: Morihiko
dialogues.text: I was getting some ore from my friend's place and happened to bump into them on the way over.

dialogues.speaker: Morihiko
dialogues.text: I think their leader's name was Keisuke, just like you said.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Just as I thought! Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: If Sakujirou still hasn't made up his mind, those two running into each other won't solve anything — and even worse, there'll be no coming back from it for Sakujirou.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: #We can't let that happen. Come with me, {NICKNAME}, let's track them down!

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Kaori
dialogues.text: Thank you, dears. *sigh* Sorry to make you run errands for us.

dialogues.speaker: Imatani Saburou
dialogues.text: I'll brew some tea and prepare some snacks for when you get back.

dialogues.speaker: Matsuzaka
dialogues.text: That man who just came past looked really scary...

dialogues.speaker: Saika
dialogues.text: Do you think... they're here to steal our weapons?

dialogues.speaker: Iwao
dialogues.text: Oh... So we won't be able to scare off the Great Mujina Youkai anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: Hehe, she's always full of life.

dialogues.speaker: Naganohara Ryuunosuke
dialogues.text: That's my girl, that's my girl...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, these plants are getting a little out of control.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, but this is someone's place, isn't it... Guess we can't go chopping everything down...

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Now that we've finished all the chores, it's time to talk to the Imatanis about Sakujirou.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: *sigh* Well, can't say we didn't try.

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: I'll let Sakujirou know after we get back.
